Regression proofs on a record's components: a method of a record, or one taking or returning a record of primitives, is proved with the record built from symbolic components in both versions; examples 126 and 127 on a new backoff kernel (verification pending)
Regression proofs relate a static method to the record's method it became, and leave trivial callees as written; examples 128 and 129 on the batch commit kernel (verification pending)

Regression proofs build the previous version's record from the new parameters: a record whose components changed, or a record's method made static, is related by a constructor call among --before-arguments; examples 130 and 131 on the backoff record gaining a multiplier (verification pending)

The tool's own checker asks the solver once per branch: each path carries a model of its condition, a condition taken before costs nothing, and records are in its fragment; examples 132 and 133 on the token bucket's refill (verification pending)

Regression proofs relate a record result whose components changed, or a result that became a record, by a relation over the components; examples 134 and 135 on a new window-counter kernel of Crosscut (verification pending)

The tool's own checker leaves a division to the solver under cheap facts and builds its circuit only where a model got it wrong, and does not wait for an undecided branch side; examples 136 and 137 on the window counter's start aligned by a mask (verification pending)

The tool's own checker leaves a multiplication to the solver under cheap facts and rewrites a quotient times its divisor as the dividend less the remainder; examples 138 and 139 on the window start as the window's index times its length (verification pending)

The tool's own checker takes arrays of primitives into its fragment: a cell per index up to the bound, reads as a choice among the cells, writes as conditional updates, bounds and sizes as exception branches; examples 140 and 141 on the lookupswitch bisection rewritten half-open (verification pending)

The tool's own checker merges paths where they meet once a search has grown past a few hundred, keeping the models of every path merged; examples 142 and 143 on the constant-pool encoder's ASCII fast path, the proof that waited for a larger machine (verification pending)

A regression or property proof that covers no input says so: the statement is probed with its calls replaced by the assertion's failure, and a scope or assumption every input satisfies, or an array bound below what the scope asks, is reported as vacuous; examples 144 and 145 on a short-table scan of the lookupswitch search (verification pending)
